adoption.body: Businesses in the Census Bureau's survey report current AI use at 21.8%. Expected use within six months is 25.9%, but the measure records stated intent rather than current use. Near-term expectations therefore remain close to the current-use base.
adoption.headline: Business AI intentions sit just above reported current use

compute.body: Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, with capacity utilization at 81.7%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%, but utilization was lower at 72.2%. Output is rising in both industries, while the utilization gap indicates different pressure on installed capacity.
compute.headline: Compute output is growing under different capacity conditions

data_center.body: Available project records list 3,068 operating sites and 1,556 sites in development, a ratio of 0.51. Separately, 894 sites are tracked in the active pipeline. Meta is reportedly planning a further expansion of its Eagle Mountain campus in Utah, providing a current example of continued campus expansion without establishing the pace of the wider pipeline. These site counts describe the breadth of activity, not the power or compute capacity the projects will deliver.
data_center.headline: Project records show one development site for every two operating sites, with 894 sites tracked as active

finance.body: Operating cash flow is 1.42 times current CapEx, while cash reserves are equivalent to 0.96 years at the current spending pace. Borrower strain is 26.0, while lender strain is -13.5. The funding picture therefore combines cash-flow coverage above current CapEx with reserve coverage below one year and strain readings of opposite signs.
finance.headline: Cash flow covers current CapEx, but reserves alone fall short of a year

grid_storage.body: The active queue contains 2,061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, but only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages. Earlier experience cautions against reading the full queue as future operating supply: only 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. That historical outcome is not a forecast for the current queue. Pennsylvania regulators are reportedly preparing to consider ratemaking, return on equity and curtailment as data-center load grows, putting pricing and operating rules alongside the physical buildout.
grid_storage.headline: The 2,061-GW grid queue remains mostly outside advanced stages

macro.body: Financial signals are mixed rather than uniformly weak. The AI Equity Index and average sector trading pressure edged lower, yet 61.3% of covered companies remain positive over one year and the median return increased to 14.8%. Operating cash flow equals 1.42 times current CapEx, while cash reserves equal 0.96 years of spending. Borrower strain is 26.0, compared with lender strain of -13.5. The funding picture combines support from current internal cash generation with a sub-one-year reserve cushion and divergent borrower and lender conditions. Physical expansion is visible in current output as well as project records. Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, and semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%. Data-center records show 0.51 development site per operating site, while 894 sites are tracked in the active pipeline. Yet only 24.2% of the 2,061-GW active interconnection queue is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 cohort reached operation. The historical rate is not a forecast, but it cautions against treating proposed capacity as delivered supply. Pennsylvania regulators are reportedly considering ratemaking, returns and curtailment as data-center load grows, a reminder that grid expansion also requires decisions about prices and operating rules. Broad deployment remains gradual. Current AI use is reported by 23.2% of businesses, compared with 27.3% expecting use within six months, a 4.1-point gap. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, and the strongest channel is growing 0.8%. Nonfarm-business productivity is growing 2.2%, but that aggregate does not identify an AI contribution. For now, the evidence is clearer on infrastructure activity than on broad labor-market or productivity effects.
macro.headline: Physical buildout continues, but pipeline conversion and broad deployment remain limited

market.body: The AI Equity Index slipped to 32.2 and average sector trading pressure to 50.0. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns also edged down to 61.3%, but the median one-year return increased to 14.8%. The combination shows softer breadth without a uniform deterioration in company-level performance.
market.headline: Market indicators edge lower, but the median one-year return improves

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index edged up to 32.5, and average sector trading pressure rose more materially to 52.0. Positive one-year returns now cover 62.7% of tracked companies, while the median one-year return eased to 14.2%. Breadth has improved, but the lower median return keeps the signal from being uniformly stronger.

headline.text: Market breadth improves even as the typical one-year return eases

body.text: The Chicago Fed NFCI is -0.56, consistent with looser-than-average financial conditions, and its three-month change remains slightly negative at -0.05. Borrower strain is 26.0, compared with lender strain of -13.5. The Federal Reserve nevertheless raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.0%. In deal financing, banks reportedly provided a $22 billion chip loan for a Blackstone-Alphabet AI cloud venture, while Oracle’s $18 billion of data-center debt was separately reported under pressure. The contrast shows that large financings remain possible while individual capital structures can still come under strain.

headline.text: Financial conditions remain loose overall, but large infrastructure deals show uneven strain

body.text: Output grew 9.2% in computers and peripherals and 11.5% in semiconductors and electronic components. Capacity utilization was much higher in computers and peripherals, at 81.7%, than in semiconductors, at 72.2%, so the production gains are occurring under different degrees of pressure on installed capacity. Taiwan also broke ground on an advanced-packaging park anchored by TSMC, adding a current example of investment at the packaging stage that the broad utilization figures do not isolate.

The measure adds a near-term state-level constraint, although the report does not establish how many tracked sites it affects.

body.text: The active interconnection queue contains 2,061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, but only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages. Just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation; that history is a warning against treating the full queue as delivered supply, not a forecast for the current cohort. Texas regulators reportedly adopted softened rules for data-center interconnection. Microsoft is also reported to be preserving its ability to challenge a decision on data-center transmission costs, indicating that connection terms and cost allocation remain unsettled alongside the physical backlog.

headline.text: The grid queue remains vast but early-stage as Texas adjusts data-center interconnection rules

body.text: Current AI use is reported by 23.2% of businesses, and 27.3% expect to use it within six months, leaving a 4.1-point gap between present use and stated intent. Among adults age 18–64, 61.8% report some generative-AI use. The measures are not directly comparable, but they show much broader exposure among individuals than reported current use across businesses.

headline.text: Consumer generative-AI use is widespread, while business use remains narrower
AI infrastructure is expanding amid deal-level financing pressure and project-delivery constraints

paragraphs.text: Broad financial conditions do not point to a generalized funding squeeze. At -0.56, the Chicago Fed NFCI remains consistent with looser-than-average conditions, and its three-month change is slightly negative at -0.05. Lender strain is -13.5, while borrower strain is higher at 26.0. The Federal Reserve nonetheless raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.0%. Banks reportedly provided $22 billion for a Blackstone-Alphabet chip and AI cloud venture, while Oracle’s $18 billion of data-center debt was reported under pressure. Very large financings can still clear, but scale does not remove deal-level risk.

Physical supply is still expanding. Output is growing 9.2% in computers and peripherals and 11.5% in semiconductors and electronic components, while Taiwan has broken ground on an advanced-packaging park anchored by TSMC. Available data-center records list 1,556 development sites against 3,068 operating sites, with 894 active pipeline sites tracked separately. These measures show broad activity, but they do not specify the amount of compute or power that will ultimately be delivered.

Converting plans into operating capacity remains the central uncertainty. Only 24.2% of the 2,061-GW interconnection queue has reached executed-agreement or construction stages. Just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort became operational, a caution rather than a forecast for current projects. Texas regulators reportedly softened data-center interconnection rules even as the governor broadened a moratorium on approvals to include environmental permits. Microsoft is also preserving its ability to challenge a decision on data-center transmission costs. The reports show that connection terms, permitting and cost allocation must be resolved alongside the physical buildout.

End-use adoption remains uneven. Businesses report current AI use at 23.2%, versus 27.3% expecting use within six months, a 4.1-point gap. By comparison, 61.8% of adults age 18–64 report some generative-AI use. The measures cover different populations and types of use, but the contrast suggests that individual experimentation is much more widespread than organizational adoption.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions.
